headline.text: Helsingin kaupunki's crude recorded MDT share is 0.1% (95% CI 0.0–0.4; n=1/1486) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, measuring recording practice, not care.

details.text: For recorded MDT meetings, Helsingin kaupunki's crude share of 0.1% (95% CI 0.0–0.4; n=1/1486) has a 95% confidence interval that excludes the national value of 6.0% (893/14873), reflecting that specialist procedures enter HILMO only from direct patient contacts rather than comprehensive multidisciplinary review.

Among overlapping treatment categories where a patient can have several, Helsingin kaupunki's crude symptomatic treatment share is 34.5% (95% CI 32.1–37.0; n=513/1486), with a 95% confidence interval excluding the national 39.5% (5871/14873), while crude curative treatment is 33.0% (95% CI 30.7–35.5; n=491/1486), excluding the national 27.0% (4009/14873) from above.

In the remaining overlapping categories where a patient can have several, the crude life-prolonging treatment share is 30.8% (95% CI 28.5–33.1; n=457/1486), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 30.4% (4522/14873), and the crude share with no treatment record within 12 months—mixing untreated patients and unrecorded treatment—is 29.1% (95% CI 26.8–31.4; n=432/1486), including the national 27.5% (4089/14873).

While county-level wait times are not in public data, preliminary unpublished national figures show an average of 155 days from first symptoms to treatment in Finland (versus 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark), comprising a 56-day patient delay, a 41-day primary care interval, and a 58-day specialist care interval.

headline.text: Taulukko 11 gives only unadjusted crude county shares, and as a separate limitation, shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

details.text: Taulukko 11 county shares are crude and not age-adjusted; age-adjusted county shares appear only in Kuva 16 (by sex, with 95% CIs), where national curative reference lines are digitised from the figure at 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (±0.5 percentage points), with no digitised Helsingin kaupunki value to test whether its curative gap holds after age adjustment.

As a separate limitation from age adjustment, treatment shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients, even though a journal article found that HILMO hospital discharge diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types regarding diagnosis concordance.

Public report data do not measure symptoms or referral dates, outpatient primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, and imaging appears only indirectly because about 20% of patients are diagnosed on clinical examination alone, such as imaging.

In specialist care, public data show that 93.6% of patients have a lung cancer visit in HILMO within 12 months and which treatment type is recorded, but not when visits or treatments started, while the HUS regional pathway document states that HUS refers patients to the MDT only when needed.

headline.text: The team recommends publishing how completely stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding are recorded, reporting access times using THL 21/2016 definitions, and standardising referrals and diagnostic-phase contacts.

details.text: Because Helsingin kaupunki's crude recorded MDT share is 0.1% (95% CI 0.0–0.4; n=1/1486) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally—measuring recording practice, not care—and stage is missing for about 48% of patients, the team recommends publishing per county how completely stage, drug treatment, and MDT meetings are recorded and reading gaps as data-quality signals first.

Since Finland has no cancer quality registry or unified national system monitoring access to care, and the Health Care Act (§52) sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion, the team recommends reporting county access times using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions (covering 16 cancers) and flagging stalled handovers until national target times exist.

Supported by mentor insight that a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating in specialist care, the team recommends a standard referral template and referring persistent unexplained symptoms after a normal X-ray to a pulmonologist, modelled on the KYS regional pathway document, while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Because regional pathway documents show no region names a diagnostic-phase contact person—with the HUS regional pathway document assigning a nurse at the first visit—the team recommends naming a contact person from referral to diagnosis, while STM roadmap measure 1.2.3 plans guidance on a named care-coordinator model by 2026–2028 for counties to adopt by 2029–2031 without specifying the care phase.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
